title: Seeing touring bands at the San Jacinto dance hall
summary: He describes the Gypsy Tea Room and the San Jacinto hall, where he saw name bands, and how it was laid out.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: So you went to the Gypsy Tea Room. Could you tell me about that? But what, what, what it, what it looked like?

Well, the thing is, uh, it, it would change from time to time. At one time it was a, uh, uh, uh, dance hall. Then it was a nightclub and it would switch. The, the, the one that I remember, uh, that I would go to and see most of the bands was at the Sanja Center. Mm-hmm. I remember when I was old enough, I saw bands like Andy Kirk, uh, I saw Lucky Milner. I saw King Colox's band. Right. I heard, uh, uh, uh, uh, Harkin's band. Uh, you know, all those bands that would come in town,
they would play there. So this is, so before you even playing music, you're absorbing. Yeah. Yeah. All this, yeah. Big band and pop music. Right. Et cetera. And you know.

The second lining. Right. All of this. Yeah. Just all of this. And the thing is that I often, uh, laugh about it, that the bands at those times were the draw. The singers were just incidental. Incidental. They would sit on the band standing when they called them up. They'd, you know. Right. Right. But now it's the other way around. The singers are the feature and the musicians are just incidental. Unfortunately. Yeah. So it goes.
Uh, so you, tell me about San Jacinto. Um, why, why was it so popular? Well, the thing is it was a,

uh, a large, it was, uh, had a larger dance floor. It, uh, was built straight back. Because, uh, if they had a name band coming in, they would be on the hot night, which would be Saturday. Mm-hmm.
